title: Getting a Job
goals: Talk about your job interests and plans with gerunds: I enjoy working with people.
Choose between a gerund and an infinitive after common verbs: I want to apply; I avoid arriving late.
Say how long you have done something with the present perfect and for / since.
Understand the main parts of an online job ad: position, requirements, salary and how to apply.
Use useful phrases with a career counselor and in a job interview.
Write a short thank-you email after a job interview.

learn.title: Gerunds (verb + -ing)
learn.html:
A gerund is the -ing form of a verb used like a noun. It is very common when we talk about jobs and skills.

UseExample
As the subject of a sentenceWorking with people is interesting.
After a preposition (in, at, of, about, for)She is good at solving problems. / I'm interested in becoming a nurse.
After some verbs: enjoy, avoid, finish, keep, consider, suggest, mind, practiceHe enjoys helping customers. / I avoid being late.
After look forward toI look forward to hearing from you.

Negative gerund: put not before it: I'm worried about not finding a job.

watch.wrong: She is good at to talk with clients.
watch.right: She is good at talking with clients.
watch.why: After a preposition, always use the -ing form.

watch.wrong: Work in a team is fun.
watch.right: Working in a team is fun.
watch.why: When a verb is the subject, use the gerund.

watch.wrong: I look forward to meet you.
watch.right: I look forward to meeting you.
watch.why: In look forward to, the word to is a preposition, so the verb takes -ing.
Enjoy is followed by a gerund, never by an infinitive.

learn.title: Gerunds and infinitives
learn.html:
Some verbs are followed by a gerund (-ing), some by an infinitive (to + base verb), and some by both. You need to learn each verb.

PatternCommon verbsExample
verb + gerundenjoy, avoid, finish, keep, consider, suggest, mind, practiceShe finished writing her résumé.
verb + infinitivewant, need, hope, plan, decide, expect, learn, would likeI decided to look for a new job.
both (same meaning)like, love, hate, start, begin, continueI like working / to work at night.
adjective + infinitivehappy to, ready to, easy to, glad toI'm ready to start tomorrow.
infinitive of purpose (why?)to + base verbHe went to the office to leave his résumé.

Tip: after a preposition, use a gerund. After want, need, hope, plan, decide, use to.

watch.wrong: I want finding a better job.
watch.right: I want to find a better job.
watch.why: Want is followed by an infinitive.

watch.wrong: She avoids to speak in meetings.
watch.why: Avoid is followed by a gerund.

watch.wrong: He went to the bank for ask about a loan.
watch.right: He went to the bank to ask about a loan.
watch.why: To explain the purpose, use to + base verb, not for + verb.

watch.wrong: They decided hiring two new workers.
watch.right: They decided to hire two new workers.
watch.why: Decide is followed by an infinitive.

learn.title: Present perfect with for and since
learn.html:
Use the present perfect (have / has + past participle) for something that started in the past and continues now. To say how long, use for or since.

WordUseExample
fora period of timeI have worked here for three years.
sincethe starting pointShe has been a nurse since 2018. / since last March.
QuestionHow long...?How long have you been a driver? — For six years.
  • Negative: I haven't had a day off since Monday.
  • Short answers: Have you worked here long? — Yes, I have.
  • The present perfect continuous is also possible: I've been working here for three years.

watch.wrong: I work in this company since 2020.
watch.right: I have worked in this company since 2020.
watch.why: For an action that continues until now, use the present perfect, not the simple present.

watch.wrong: She has been unemployed since two months.
watch.right: She has been unemployed for two months.
watch.why: Use for with a period of time; since is for a starting point.

watch.wrong: How long do you work here?
watch.right: How long have you worked here?

watch.why: 2015 is a starting point, so use since.

learn.title: Useful expressions
learn.html:
• I'm interested in working in... / I'd like some advice about... — talking to a career counselor.
  • What are you good at? / What do you enjoy doing? — questions a counselor may ask.
  • Have you ever thought about...? — suggesting an idea politely.
  • I suggest updating your résumé. — giving advice.
  • Tell me about yourself. / Why do you want this job? — common interview questions.
  • I have three years of experience in... / I've worked as a... since... — talking about your experience.
  • I'm good at working under pressure. — talking about your strengths.
  • Thank you for your time. / I look forward to hearing from you. — closing an interview or an email.

write.model:
Subject: Thank you for the interview

Dear Ms. Herrera,

Thank you for meeting with me yesterday about the sales assistant position. I enjoyed learning more about your team and the plans for the new store.

I am very interested in this job. I have worked in customer service for three years, and I have always liked helping people find the right product. I believe I can learn your new system quickly, and I am happy to work on weekends if necessary.

Our conversation made me even more excited about the position. If you need more information, such as references or examples of my work, please let me know.

Thank you again for your time. I look forward to hearing from you.

Sincerely,
Ana Torres

reading.title: Men, Women and Jobs
reading.intro: Read the article about changing ideas on jobs and answer.
paragraphs: Many years ago, people often said that some jobs were only for men and other jobs were only for women. Nurses and secretaries were usually women, and pilots, mechanics and engineers were usually men. Today this idea is changing, but slowly.

Look at some examples. Sofia has been a truck driver for eight years. She enjoys traveling, and she is proud of driving big vehicles safely. At first, some customers were surprised when they saw her, but now they respect her work. Her company has hired three more women drivers since 2020.

Daniel has worked as a nurse since 2017. He decided to study nursing because he wanted to help people. He says that the hardest part was hearing jokes from his friends. Now he is a team leader in a hospital, and he has trained more than twenty young nurses.

Experts say that children learn about jobs from the people around them. When parents talk about work in a fair way, children feel free to choose any career. Schools can help too. A good career counselor avoids saying "this is a job for boys" or "this is a job for girls." Instead, the counselor asks about interests and skills.

Of course, changes take time. Some companies still prefer to hire people who look like their current workers. Others are learning that mixed teams solve problems better. Many workers also want to have flexible schedules, so they can take care of their families. This is important for both men and women.

In the end, the best question is not "Is this job for a man or a woman?" It is "Do I like doing this work, and am I good at it?" People who follow their interests usually work harder and feel happier. Everyone benefits when talented people can choose the job they really want.

listening.title: At the career counselor's office
listening.intro: Listen to the conversation between a career counselor and a client. You can repeat it.

lines.text: Good morning, Marco. Please sit down. How can I help you today?
Good morning. I have worked in a warehouse for four years, but I want to find a different job.
I see. What do you enjoy doing most at work?
I like using computers, and I enjoy helping people solve problems.
That's useful. Have you ever thought about working in customer service?
Yes, I've considered it. But I haven't studied English since high school.
Don't worry. Many companies need people who can speak some English. You could take a course in the evenings.
That sounds good. How long does a course take?
Usually about six months. Meanwhile, I suggest updating your résumé and practicing for interviews.
I'm not very good at talking about myself. Is that a problem?
Not at all. We can practice together every Friday. Are you free this Friday at ten?
Yes, I'm free. Thank you so much for your help!
